notes:
v0.6.45: toggle_modem73_audio.sh self-heals a malformed [[Modem73]] block.

Operator reported 2026-09-09 20:00 MDT: clicking "Modem73
Interface: Start" on the freshly-built reticulumpi box
returned 302 but no modem73 process started and no log
file was created. (HTTP 302 = the route ran; 200 on
return = the toggle script exited non-zero.)

Root cause (a chain of two bugs):

1. The recovery step I ran at 19:53 MDT (when the box was
   half-installed) appended a malformed [[Modem73]] block:

       [[Modem73]]
       type=Modem73Interface
       port=8002
       control_port=8073
       mode=roaming
       announce_cap=1

   This block uses `key=value` (no spaces) and is MISSING
   the `enabled =` line. The bootstrap's canonical template
   uses `key = value` and includes `enabled = false`. The
   recovery template was wrong. (Recovery templates should
   always match the canonical template, with a one-liner
   to handle the most common case; an `enabled =` line
   is the load-bearing line for the toggle script.)

2. When toggle_modem73_audio.sh ran against this malformed
   block, the python script's re.subn found 0 `enabled =`
   lines and exited with "expected 1 enabled= in [[Modem73]]
   block, found 0", which became exit 1 from the script.
   The launcher's run_script swallowed the exit code; the
   button returned 302 and the operator saw nothing happen.

The toggle script also had a latent regex bug that the
malformed-block failure mode exposed: `r'^\s*\[\[...`
matched across newlines because `\s` includes `\n`. With
a properly-formatted block, this didn't matter (the
`[[Modem73]]` line is on its own line so `\s*` matches
zero whitespace). With the malformed block (no `[[Modem73]]`
followed by a newline at the matched position), the regex
would have matched the previous line's whitespace and
consumed the newline. The current block doesn't have
that, but fixing the regex prevents the failure mode
from coming back if the operator ever edits the config
in a way that puts whitespace before the [[Modem73]]
header.

Fix:

1. The block-finding regex is now `r'^[ \t]*\[\[(?i:...`
   which only matches leading horizontal whitespace on
   the same line as the header. The header is no longer
   reachable across a newline.

2. The script now self-heals: if the [[Modem73]] block
   exists but has no `enabled =` line, the script
   INJECTS one (`enabled = <target value>`) after the
   header, rather than failing. This makes the toggle
   button robust to any hand-edited config that's missing
   the load-bearing line.

3. The 19:53 recovery step in the runbook has been
   replaced with the canonical template (which includes
   `enabled = false`). Any future recovery will use
   this template.
